findings.message: Line carries two distinct normative obligations under a single @prd: PRD.01.09.d101 tag: (1) the count-delta + timing obligation (increment by exactly one WITHIN the visit-count reconciliation window) and (2) an exactly-once / idempotency obligation (duplicate delivery of the same event SHALL NOT produce a second increment). These are independently testable rules and should each be a separate atomic line with its own @prd tag.
findings.recommendation: Split into two lines, both tagged @prd: PRD.01.09.d101: line A keeps the WHEN-served increment-by-exactly-one obligation with the reconciliation-window WITHIN; line B states the event-driven exactly-once / no-double-increment obligation (deduplication mechanism owned by the visit-observability ADR topic, BRD.01.08.c478). Retain the cross-reference to EARS.01.03.f766 for the concurrent-no-loss counterpart.

findings.message: Primary obligation is atomic, but the line carries a trailing normative sentence ('A duplicate submission … MAY return … either outcome SHALL satisfy the code-to-URL uniqueness invariant (EARS.01.03.bca8)'). The embedded SHALL slightly muddies the single-rule-per-line boundary, though the clause explicitly defers ownership to the ubiquitous uniqueness rule bca8 and reads as a consistency restatement rather than an independent obligation.
findings.recommendation: Optional: demote the duplicate-submission sentence to a non-normative note (e.g., 'Note: a duplicate submission may reuse or reissue a code; uniqueness is owned by EARS.01.03.bca8') so the line carries exactly one SHALL obligation. No new @prd tag required since bca8 already owns the invariant.

findings.location: EARS.01.03.eca5 — Capacity-utilization alert (WITHIN the capacity-monitoring envelope)
findings.message: The WITHIN timing bound 'the capacity-monitoring envelope' carries no @threshold tag or named-ADR deferral marker of its own. The present threshold governs the utilization level, not the alert-emit latency, so an engineer could read the alert-cadence bound as resolved when it is actually an unstated/deferred timing bound.
findings.recommendation: Attach an explicit threshold or named-ADR deferral marker for the alert-emit timing envelope (e.g., a @threshold for capacity-monitoring alert latency, or name the owning ADR topic for the alert cadence) so the timing bound is unambiguously deferred rather than implicitly resolved by the utilization-level threshold.
